suggestion.simple_explanation: Task A is a maintainability ticket: the program's 'Qt wrapper selection info' record (which explains how qutebrowser chose between PyQt5/PyQt6) currently stores the selection reason as a free-text string and always prints two lines saying 'PyQt5: not tried' / 'PyQt6: not tried' even when no wrapper import was ever attempted. A asks to replace the free-text reason with a fixed set of named values (an enumeration) and to stop printing the 'not tried' placeholder lines, so the text output of this record shows only which wrapper was picked and why. Task B is a separate, cosmetic ticket about the same text output: the two 'PyQt5:' and 'PyQt6:' lines are listed in the wrong order (PyQt5 first) even though the project's preferred wrapper order is PyQt6 first, and the section header 'Qt wrapper:' should be capitalized to 'Qt Wrapper:' to match the style of the other sections in the version report. Both tickets force edits to the exact same function - the text-formatting method (__str__) of the SelectionInfo class in qutebrowser/qt/machinery.py - and their desired outputs for that same function cannot both be true: A's output must contain no PyQt lines at all in the default state, while B's output must contain reordered/renamed PyQt lines.
suggestion.shared_region: qutebrowser/qt/machinery.py, class SelectionInfo - specifically the __str__ method (and the pyqt5/pyqt6/reason dataclass fields it renders). A rewrites __str__ to build a line list, omit pyqt5/pyqt6 lines when no outcome was recorded (fields become Optional[str] = None), and render reason via an enum's .value; B rewrites the same __str__ to emit the header as 'Qt Wrapper:' and the two PyQt lines in PyQt6-then-PyQt5 order.
suggestion.taskA: SelectionInfo uses free-form string values for selection reasons, which is error-prone and hard to validate. Introduce a public SelectionReason enumeration (CLI, ENV, AUTO, DEFAULT, FAKE, UNKNOWN) and use it for SelectionInfo.reason; render the reason via its enumerated value in the string form. Also, the string form must omit the 'PyQt5: ...' / 'PyQt6: ...' lines when no import outcome was recorded for that wrapper - the current 'not tried' default is a stale placeholder that must be replaced by a value (e.g. None) that suppresses the line. A SelectionInfo built without explicit pyqt5/pyqt6 arguments must render exactly: 'Qt wrapper:\nselected: <wrapper> (via <reason>)', and when the reason is FAKE the trailing line must read 'selected: <wrapper> (via fake)'.
suggestion.taskB: The Qt wrapper section in the version report (produced by str(SelectionInfo)) is inconsistent with the rest of the report: the section header is lowercase 'Qt wrapper:' while every other section is capitalized, and the per-wrapper outcome lines list PyQt5 before PyQt6 even though the project's wrapper preference order (and the WRAPPERS list) is PyQt6 first. Reorder the lines to PyQt6 then PyQt5 and capitalize the header to 'Qt Wrapper:' so the version output reads consistently.
suggestion.independence_rationale: B is a plausible standalone cosmetic/reporting ticket: a maintainer looking at the :version output could independently file 'the Qt wrapper block is misordered and its header is inconsistent with the other sections' without any knowledge of the enum refactor. It is motivated by the report's presentation, not by type safety or the 'not tried' placeholder. Caveat: B is close to the same complaint family as A (both touch the placeholder lines), so its independence is real but modest - it must be framed strictly as an ordering/capitalization fix, not as 'fix the not tried placeholder', or it degenerates into a competing solution of A rather than an independent ticket.
suggestion.conflict: Both solutions rewrite SelectionInfo.__str__ in incompatible ways. A's version conditionally omits the PyQt5/PyQt6 lines entirely (default state renders exactly two lines) and keeps the header 'Qt wrapper:'; B's version keeps both PyQt lines, reorders them, and renames the header. Naively merging (concatenating or auto-merging the two __str__ bodies) yields a single method that either still emits the placeholder lines A's tests forbid, or drops/reorders the lines B's tests require - the combined suite fails. The dataclass fields also collide: A changes pyqt5/pyqt6 from str='not tried' to Optional[str]=None and reason from Optional[str] to an enum, while B's solution assumes the old str fields and old reason strings.
suggestion.reconciliation_sketch:
One coherent __str__ that adopts A's data model (Optional pyqt5/pyqt6 with None meaning 'not recorded', reason as SelectionReason rendered via .value) and B's presentation where lines are present: emit the header in B's capitalized form, list recorded wrapper outcomes in PyQt6-then-PyQt5 order, and omit any wrapper with no recorded outcome. The default-state output then stays exactly A's two-line form (satisfying A's 'MUST render exactly' requirement, since B's ordering only constrains the relative order of lines that are actually emitted), while a fully-populated SelectionInfo shows 'Qt Wrapper:
PyQt6: ...
PyQt5: ...
selected: ...' (satisfying B).
suggestion.test_strategy: A's set: the existing tests/unit/test_qt_machinery.py (updated to construct SelectionInfo with SelectionReason.FAKE) plus tests/unit/utils/test_version.py::test_version_info, whose expected output drops the two 'not tried' lines. B's set: new unit tests in tests/unit/test_qt_machinery.py asserting (1) str(SelectionInfo(wrapper='PyQt5', pyqt6='success', pyqt5='ModuleNotFoundError: ...')) lists the PyQt6 line before the PyQt5 line under a 'Qt Wrapper:' header, and (2) str(SelectionInfo(wrapper='PyQt5')) (no outcomes recorded) still renders exactly the two-line form with no PyQt lines - a constraint that only the reconciled code satisfies. Base code fails both sets (no enum; wrong order/header; placeholder lines present). A alone fails B's ordering/header tests; B alone fails A's enum and line-omission tests. The combined suite passes only on the reconciled __str__.

notes: Region facts at base commit: SelectionInfo (qutebrowser/qt/machinery.py:49-68) has pyqt5/pyqt6 defaulting to the 'not tried' placeholder, reason as Optional[str], and a __str__ that always emits both PyQt lines; the only production consumer of str(INFO) is version.version_info() (qutebrowser/utils/version.py:885), whose output is pinned by tests/unit/utils/test_version.py (the 'not tried' lines appear in its expected template at lines 1346-1347). INFO.wrapper is also read by earlyinit.check_pyqt/check_libraries and the USE_*/IS_* constants in init(), but those only touch .wrapper, not the string form. A's fail_to_pass set includes the whole test_version_info parameterization because the test patch changed the expected template, not because version.py changed. The contradictory pairing is the stronger of the two, but its B is a cosmetic reordering of the very lines A's spec says must disappear, so B's independence is the weak link (confidence 2). The complementary pairing (Unavailable message + reason) is a real, small interface, but the contract is thin and B's pre-A failure depends on B being written enum-dependent (confidence 1). Neither pairing is a decomposition of A: B's tickets are framed around report presentation and error debuggability, not around the enum refactor itself.

suggestion.simple_explanation: Task A (the original ticket) fixes a crash on Linux with QtWebEngine 5.15.3: when the system locale has no matching Chromium translation file (.pak), the browser shows only a blank page. A adds a hidden workaround that, when a boolean setting is on, computes a safe fallback language and passes it to the browser engine as a --lang=... startup argument. Task B (an independent, plausible ticket) would add a user-facing setting to force a specific --lang=... value for any user, on any OS, because some users want to pin the interface language regardless of their system locale. Both tasks must edit the same small region: the function in qutebrowser/config/qtargs.py that builds the list of arguments handed to the browser engine (_qtwebengine_args). Two agents working blindly would each insert their own --lang line into that function, producing a duplicated/conflicting --lang argument (Chromium honors the last one, so the workaround could be silently overridden by the user flag or vice versa), and a test asserting exactly one --lang argument fails on the naive merge. A single reconciled change yields --lang exactly once: the explicit user setting wins when set, otherwise the 5.15.3 workaround value is used.
suggestion.shared_region: qutebrowser/config/qtargs.py, function _qtwebengine_args (the block of code that appends Chromium startup arguments, around the --disable-in-process-stack-traces / --enable-logging lines where A's gold patch inserts its --lang yield)
suggestion.taskA: On Linux with QtWebEngine 5.15.3, some resolved locales have no matching Chromium .pak file, so Chromium's network service crashes and qutebrowser shows only a blank page. Add a workaround, gated by a new boolean setting qt.workarounds.locale (default off, QtWebEngine backend only): when the original locale's .pak is missing from Qt's qtwebengine_locales directory, compute a Chromium-compatible fallback (en/en-PH/en-LR->en-US, other en-*->en-GB, es-*->es-419, pt->pt-BR, other pt-*->pt-PT, zh-HK/zh-MO->zh-TW, zh/other zh-*->zh-CN, else base language) and pass it to Chromium via a --lang argument; return en-US if neither .pak exists. No docs/changelog updates in scope.
suggestion.taskB: Users on any platform who run their system in a non-English locale but want an English (or otherwise specific) UI language currently have no way to pin it: qutebrowser always passes the locale Qt resolves. Add a user-facing setting (e.g. qt.lang, String, default empty, QtWebEngine backend) that, when set, makes qutebrowser pass --lang=<value> to Chromium unconditionally, on all operating systems and all QtWebEngine versions, independent of any crash workarounds. Documented as a general locale preference, not tied to 5.15.3.
suggestion.independence_rationale: B is a feature request that stands on its own: 'let me choose the UI language' is a common, real ticket for a browser and is motivated by users, not by the 5.15.3 crash. It does not mention the workaround, the .pak files, or the version gate. The overlap is only the mechanical fact that both deliver their value by emitting a --lang argument in the same argument-building function, which is exactly the kind of same-region collision the seed is meant to model. It is not 'the other half of A' because B works on every OS/version and A only on Linux 5.15.3.
suggestion.conflict: Both patches insert a --lang=... yield into the same contiguous block of _qtwebengine_args. Naively merged, the function contains two independent --lang emissions: A's (conditional on the workaround setting + Linux + 5.15.3 + missing .pak) and B's (conditional on the user setting). The combined argument list can then contain two --lang values (Chromium uses the last, so one of the two behaviors is silently wrong) or, if an agent dedupes by keeping only one, one of the two test suites fails. A's tests assert the workaround's exact value appears; B's tests assert the user's value appears and that exactly one --lang is present.
suggestion.reconciliation_sketch: One code path computes a single effective language: if the user's explicit setting is non-empty use it; otherwise run A's _get_lang_override(workaround) logic; yield --lang=... at most once with the result. Both A's and B's tests then pass against the merged function.
suggestion.test_strategy: A's set: tests/unit/config/test_qtargs_locale_workaround.py (parametrized locale->fallback table, version/OS gates, .pak existence checks, setting-off -> no override). B's set: new tests in tests/unit/config/test_qtargs.py style — set the user lang setting, assert exactly one --lang=<value> in qtargs.qt_args output across OS/version combinations, and assert no --lang when the setting is empty. Combined suite runs both against the merged qtargs.py; the naive double-yield merge fails B's 'exactly one --lang' and/or A's value assertion, while the reconciled single-emission version passes all.

notes: Key observations from the base commit: (1) _qtwebengine_args in qutebrowser/config/qtargs.py is a single generator function where every Chromium flag is yielded — it is the natural, narrow shared region for any second --lang-emitting ticket, which is what makes the contradictory pairing structurally real. (2) The existing test file tests/unit/config/test_qtargs.py already contains many tests that call qtargs.qt_args and assert specific flags, so B's test style would be natural. (3) A's own requirements text says the change 'must leave the composition of Chromium's runtime argument list unchanged' and 'no --lang injection in _qtwebengine_args', yet the gold patch does exactly inject --lang in _qtwebengine_args and A's fail_to_pass tests validate the workaround's behavior — so that requirement line should be read as 'no other/structural changes to arg composition', not literally 'no --lang at all'; an authoring step must be careful not to let B's ticket contradict A's actual gold behavior. (4) The contradictory confidence is capped at 2 because B ('user-selectable --lang setting') is a believable but somewhat constructed ticket whose entire collision with A is one argument string in one function; the independence signal is moderate, not strong. (5) Complementary is not viable: no independent consumer of A's setting or argument exists in the codebase (accept_language headers in webenginesettings.py are a different mechanism and unrelated). (6) configdata.yml at the base commit already contains qt.workarounds.remove_service_workers, so the 'add a new qt.workarounds.* setting' pattern is well-established, which helps B's plausibility but does not create a second shared region beyond _qtwebengine_args.

suggestion.simple_explanation: Task A asks that Ansible error messages be computed lazily: the base text is stored separately, and the file/line/column details are looked up and appended every time the message is read, so the details always reflect the current source file. A plausible independent ticket B would ask for the opposite guarantee: an error's message must be fixed once at construction time and never change afterwards (deterministic, snapshot semantics), because other code (e.g. the galaxy error handler that overwrites the message, and log/exception dumps) relies on the message being stable. Both tickets must rewrite the same constructor and the same message attribute of the base error class, and the two designs cannot coexist: one requires the message to be a live computed property, the other requires it to be a plain value frozen at construction.
suggestion.shared_region: lib/ansible/errors/__init__.py, class AnsibleError: __init__ (lines 53-71) and the message attribute/property (lines 65-69, 73-77)
suggestion.taskA: Expose the originating YAML object on a public `obj` attribute of AnsibleError and compute the extended source-position details (file, line, column, offending line) lazily when the message is rendered, instead of baking them in at construction; keep `message` settable; re-raise parser errors unchanged when they already carry obj; thread obj through the vault single-value decode path.
suggestion.taskB: Make AnsibleError.message a stable, construction-time snapshot: compute the full message (base plus any extended details) exactly once in __init__ and store it as a plain instance attribute, and document/enforce that mutating the source file or the attached object afterwards must not change what str(error) returns. Add a unit test asserting message is an instance attribute (not a property) and that editing the referenced file after construction does not alter the message.
suggestion.independence_rationale: B is framed around determinism/stability of error text for logging and for downstream code that rewrites e.message (galaxy/api.py does exactly this), which is a real, separate concern from A's 'location-aware, always-current' goal. It reads as its own ticket. However, it is weak as an independent motivation because the base code already computes eagerly, so B is essentially a 'preserve current snapshot semantics' ticket filed in opposition to A's redesign — believable but contrived, and its whole point is to fight A.
suggestion.conflict: A's patch turns message into a property backed by _message that re-reads obj.ansible_pos and re-opens the source file on every access; B's patch keeps/forces self.message to be a plain attribute assigned once in __init__. Both edits occupy the same lines of __init__ and the same name. Naively merging yields either a duplicated property/attribute definition or a property whose getter returns a stale snapshot, so A's laziness tests and B's snapshot tests cannot both pass.
suggestion.reconciliation_sketch: Keep A's lazy property (it already yields deterministic output for a fixed file state, satisfying B's real concern) and satisfy B's testable demand by documenting that the message is a pure function of (base message, obj, file contents) and by adding a test that the message is identical across repeated reads with an unchanged file; drop B's 'must be a plain attribute' requirement as the losing side of the collision.
suggestion.test_strategy: A's set: the three fail_to_pass tests (test_load_task_kv_form_error_36848, test_vault_encrypted_unicode_forwards_obj_to_vault_decrypt, test_vault_lib_decrypt_forwards_obj_to_raised_error) plus a laziness test (modify the source file after construction, assert message changes). B's set: a test asserting type(e).__mro__ has no 'message' data descriptor (i.e. plain attribute) and that the message does not change after the file is edited. Combined suite passes only on the reconciled lazy-property design that also proves read-stability; the naive merge fails both sides.

notes: Base-commit verification: AnsibleError.__init__ stores _obj and computes self.message eagerly (errors/__init__.py:53-71); task.py:224 and helpers.py:126 read e._obj; objects.py:120 data calls self.vault.decrypt(self._ciphertext) with no obj; vault __init__.py:652/666 decrypt signatures lack obj; constructor.py:112-114 never sets ansible_pos on AnsibleVaultEncryptedUnicode; display.warning already supports formatted=True. A's three fail_to_pass tests genuinely fail on base (AttributeError on .obj, captured obj is None, TypeError on decrypt(obj=...)). Contradictory family is the stronger structural fit (both designs must own AnsibleError.__init__/message), but the best B motivation is contrived (preserve eager snapshot semantics vs A's laziness), hence low confidence. Complementary family has a real producer/consumer seam (data -> decrypt -> exc.obj) but A's problem statement already claims the vault decode path, so B risks being judged a decomposition; the config-manager locality framing is the most independent angle available. Neither family is ready-made; both need authoring work to be sound.
